subject: Hosted API — data termination windows and retention cutoff Q&A
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novatek.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: security@novatek.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novatek security questionnaire — data residency / deletion clarifications

Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our short security questionnaire — two follow-ups we want to confirm before we proceed to SSO/contracting:

1) For Hosted API calls, what is the end-to-end timeline from a customer-initiated data deletion request to the removal of all copies (primary storage, caches, and backups)? Please call out typical windows and any retained snapshots.

2) We use short-lived conversation caches on our side. Does Redwood hold any KV/prefix caches for hosted requests beyond a per-request ephemeral cache? If so, how are those cut off/evicted when a tenant requests deletion?

We left a couple of items blank in the PDF; sending it back with those flagged. Appreciate a clear operational description and any runbooks that would be relevant.

Liam O'Connor
Security Lead — Novatek Systems
liam.oconnor@novatek.com
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novatek.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, security@novatek.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novatek security questionnaire — data residency / deletion clarifications

Hi Liam — thanks for the questions and the PDF (received). High level answers below, and I attach an annotated dataflow diagram and our standard deletion-runbook excerpt. Happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer to walk through.

Summary (short):
- Primary + short-term caches: deletion action typically completes within 24 hours (automated job to remove tenant data from live stores and in-memory caches).
- Backup snapshots: we retain daily immutable backups for 30 days by default; backups are rotated and we mark the tenant's data for deletion on the next snapshot roll-off. The practical upper bound to remove data from backups is 30 days unless contractually amended.
- Logs & telemetry: PII is redacted from application logs where possible; structured telemetry may persist for 90 days for platform health unless explicitly requested for longer retention.

Answers (detailed):
1) End-to-end timeline:
- T0 (request received): automated workflow kicks off.
- T0+0–24h: live document stores, indexes, and ephemeral caches are removed/marked for deletion. We operate a tenant-scoped garbage collection that deletes objects and invalidates model/KV prefixes.
- T0+24–72h: background processes purge residual references, update routing and tenant manifests; most systems report zero live objects by 72h.
- T0+up to 30 days: backup snapshots — tenant data remains in immutable backups until the next retention window; we treat backups as the last copy and schedule permanent removal at rotation.

2) Prefix / KV caching policy:
- Our hosted runtime uses per-request and short-lived session KV caches to accelerate autoregressive generation. Those caches are in-memory shards tied to serving instances and do not persist beyond process restart or TTL (default TTL is 1 hour).
- We also operate an optional cross-request prefix cache for some high-throughput tenants to improve latency. This caching layer is tenant-scoped, encrypted, and can be disabled or immediately invalidated as part of the deletion workflow.
- On delete request we run an immediate invalidation that clears in-memory caches and triggers eviction messages to any cross-request cache nodes. When eviction completes, we log the event and return a deletion confirmation token.

Attachments: annotated diagram and excerpt from our deletion-runbook (redwood-hostedapi-dataflow-annotated.png, deletion-runbook-snippet.txt)

If you want exact SLA language in the contract (e.g., reduce backup window to 7 days), we can propose a contract addendum.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Security Solutions — Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Novatek security questionnaire — data residency / deletion clarifications

Irene — thanks for the clear breakdown. Two quick follow-ups:

A) For the cross-request prefix cache, can you confirm whether any cache snapshots are persisted to object storage for warm-start across restarts? If so, those would be considered an additional copy.

B) On the deletion confirmation token you mentioned — is that a tenant-facing artifact we can use to audit that the workflow ran, and does it include timestamps for each stage (cache invalidation, object deletion, backup-mark)?

If helpful, we can share our expected audit fields; otherwise a short example token or sample audit record would be great.

Cheers,
Liam
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novatek.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, security@novatek.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novatek security questionnaire — data residency / deletion clarifications

Liam — quick answers and a sample audit record below. Happy to provide more examples if you need fields added.

A) Cross-request prefix cache persistence:
- We do not persist cache snapshots to long-term object storage by default. Cache warm-start across restarts is achieved via ephemeral checkpoints kept in local instance storage and pulled from a short-lived encrypted cache shard (TTL < 24h). Those shards are rotated and automatically expired.
- For customers that opt into a fast-warmup feature we can maintain encrypted persisted cache blobs in object storage; that is opt-in and will be called out in the contract/feature config. If persisted blobs are enabled for your tenant we will surface that to you and include it in the deletion workflow.

B) Deletion confirmation & audit token:
- We issue an audit record per deletion request. A sample (redacted) record fields we return via the console / API:
  - request_id: 86f9b2d4
  - tenant_id: novatek-prod
  - received_at: 2026-06-28T09:14:10Z
  - caches_invalidated_at: 2026-06-28T09:14:32Z
  - objects_deleted_at: 2026-06-29T01:06:01Z
  - backups_marked_for_purge: 2026-06-29T01:06:10Z
  - completion_estimate: 2026-07-28T00:00:00Z (backup rotation date)
  - operator_runbook_ref: RBW-DEL-2026-3

- We can surface these fields through the console, an audit log export (CSV/JSON), or via a webhook to your security mailbox. The request_id is immutable and serves as the audit token you can use for cross-checks.

Next steps if this looks good:
- We can provide an ILP to shorten backup retention to 7 days for enterprise customers (requires an addendum).
- If you'd like, Karthik can run a short engineering walkthrough of the cache invalidation flow this Friday (30 min).

Thanks — I will also drop the sample audit JSON into the Drive link I shared.

Best,
Irene
